title: MarkdownX endpoints are exposed without an access-control wrapper
reasoning: The project mounts the third-party MarkdownX URLconf directly at /markdownx/. MarkdownX commonly provides editor support endpoints such as image upload/preview helpers intended for authenticated editor/admin workflows, but this include is not guarded by login, staff, or application-specific permissions at the project URL layer. If the included MarkdownX views are not independently locked down by configuration or middleware, unauthenticated network users can reach those endpoints and potentially upload content or exercise markdown processing outside the intended editor surface.
recommendation: Wrap or replace the MarkdownX routes with authenticated/staff-only views, or configure the package so any upload/processing endpoint enforces the same permissions as the editor pages that use it. At minimum, add an integration test that anonymous requests to the mounted MarkdownX endpoints are rejected.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this route, and the excerpt does not show any assertion that /markdownx/ endpoints require authentication or staff privileges.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a URL-level security test that an anonymous client POST to the MarkdownX upload endpoint under /markdownx/ returns 302/401/403, and that an authorized editor user can still use it.
minimumFixScope: Restrict the /markdownx/ include or its upload/processing views to authenticated editor/admin users, then add route-level permission tests.
